items.body:
Sensei, the  Portuguese retail intelligence company which transforms physical spaces into Conscious Spaces, today unveils its technology in a new Muffato Go store in Curitiba, Brazil. Developed in partnership with Grupo Muffato, one of Brazil’s leading supermarket groups, the store shows how AI helps retailers see, understand and act on everything happening across their store operations.
While Sensei first became known for its autonomous store technology, the intelligence behind those stores has always been designed to address a broader challenge: giving physical retail the ability and the data to understand and automate its own operations in real time. The new Muffato Go will put that capability into practice, showing how the same underlying technology can improve shelf availability, detect losses, automate checkout, manage fresh products and support online order fulfillment.
Headquartered in Portugal and operating across Europe and Brazil, Sensei has deployed its technology in more than 100 autonomous points of sale, including the world’s largest autonomous store, opened in Leiria, Portugal, in 2025. These environments have provided a demanding real-world setting in which to develop and refine its computer vision and proprietary AI models, built specifically for retail.
“The new Muffato Go shows what AI can already do in a physical store. Shoppers get a faster, simpler way to buy, but that is only the visible part. Our models recognise products and shopper interactions as they happen, and store teams get the right task at the right time. The real value is turning what happens in the store into intelligence that supports the entire business, from the shop floor to the head office. That is what we mean by Conscious Spaces: physical spaces that see, understand and act,” says Vasco Portugal, CEO and co-founder of Sensei.
Combining computer vision, deep learning, neural networks and sensor fusion, Sensei’s technology recognises products and pseudonymized customer interactions, builds virtual shopping baskets and enables customers to complete purchases without scanning items individually, by associating the items to a token that represents the customer at the checkout
“Innovation and the willingness to take bold steps are part of who we are. We are committed to making retail increasingly efficient, and the new generation of MGO reflects that ambition: using technology to enhance the shopping experience. With four years of work together with Sensei, that same technology now gives us a clearer view of how the store operates, from the shelf to the checkout,” says Everton Muffato, Director at Grupo Muffato.
Advances in AI-integrated technology also allow the system to handle variable-weight products, extending the experience to fresh produce and bakery items. Beyond the customer journey, the same intelligence alerts store teams when products need replenishing, helps identify losses in real time, and provides more accurate information to support stock management, store layout and online order preparation.
Over the past years, Sensei has continued to develop its proprietary AI models, improving product recognition, and following hundreds of shopper interactions at the same time. Its technology turns real-time observations into practical insights, helping retailers move beyond monitoring individual events to understanding how their stores operate and where action is needed.
The partnership between Sensei and Grupo Muffato began in 2022, with the Muffato Go concept in Curitiba, Sensei’s first deployment outside Europe. Four years later, Grupo Muffato is turning Muffato Go into a new business model for the group, and the new store, which Muffato describes as the largest autonomous store in Latin America, marks the next step in that evolution.
For Sensei, autonomous checkout is one application of a wider vision for physical retail. Through its proprietary computer vision technology and AI models developed specifically for the sector, the company is building Conscious Spaces: physical environments that can see what is happening, understand how they operate, and act on that knowledge.

items.body:
Omega Pressery, the UK’s only avocado-oil-focused brand, is launching on Ocado and entering foodservice through leading wholesalers Vegetarian Express and Classic Fine Foods, marking a significant next step in the growth of the business.
The launches come as the two-year-old brand grows from around 50 distribution points at launch in 2024 to more than 900 today across retail, foodservice and international markets. Revenue has grown tenfold year on year, with the business on track to surpass £1m in annual recurring revenue (ARR) before the end of 2026.
To support its next phase of growth, Omega Pressery has also secured a six-figure investment from seasoned FMCG investor Giles Brook, whose previous investments include Surreal, Vita Coco, Pip & Nut, Bio&Me, Dalston’s and Freja. Brook is joining the business in an advisory position, with the investment set to support further growth across retail, foodservice and international markets, alongside increased marketing, team growth and new product development.
From Ocado baskets, to Oddbox to foodservice
Omega Pressery launched on Ocado this week with two SKUs, with a further two due by the end of the year. The listing adds to its presence in Waitrose, Fortnum & Mason and Planet Organic, while the brand has been consistently the UK’s number-one avocado oil seller on Amazon since April 2026. A partnership with fruit and vegetable subscription service Oddbox has also taken its products directly into more consumers’ homes.
The foodservice launch gives chefs and operators access to Omega Pressery’s versatile range through Vegetarian Express and Classic Fine Foods, including Light Avocado Oil in 1L and 5L formats. With a neutral flavour and 270°C smoke point, Light Avocado Oil is suited to high-heat cooking and frying, while Extra Virgin Avocado Oil offers a high smoke point of 240°C making it versatile for cooking, whilst its subtle flavour allows it to be a suitable option for dressings and finishing.
The launches come as the UK avocado oil category continues to grow. NIQ data shows volume sales increased by 28% between April 2024 and April 2026, while value sales rose by 33%, compared with just 1% growth across other oils. Avocado oil still accounts for less than 1% of the UK oil market, leaving significant headroom for further growth across retail and foodservice.
Internationally, Omega Pressery has secured a presence in Kenyan retail and is preparing to launch on Amazon EU, Ireland as well as Eastern Asia through Singapore.
Investment to build a category, not just a brand
Brook’s investment comes as Omega Pressery looks to capitalise on growing interest in avocado oil while developing a more transparent and traceable supply chain from East Africa.
Giles Brook said: “Omega Pressery is one of the most exciting businesses I’ve seen in recent years, and I’m delighted to be joining Niki and Niheer for the journey ahead. From our very first conversations, I was struck by the clarity of their vision and their entrepreneurial ambition.
They are building a business with genuine purpose and integrity, creating a truly differentiated brand while developing a supply chain that sets a new standard for the avocado category. Omega Pressery has all the ingredients to become a category-defining business.”
Nikita Dawda, co-founder of Omega Pressery, said: “We first met Giles through the Brand Growth Heroes Mini MBA programme and quickly realised how aligned we were on the opportunity to grow Omega Pressery while staying true to our values.
With new listings including Ocado and our launch into foodservice, alongside growing momentum with retailers such as Waitrose, we’re at a pivotal point in the business. We were deliberate about who we wanted alongside us, and Giles’ experience with Vita Coco and the coconut value chain is particularly relevant as we navigate the complexities of building a responsible, fully traceable avocado supply chain from East Africa.
Our ambition is to become the home of all things avocado. By focusing on one value chain, we’re building a stronger, more resilient supply chain alongside a growing pipeline of value-added avocado products. Giles understands what it takes to build a category, not just a brand, and his experience and belief in what we’re building make him an incredibly valuable partner. Ultimately, when retailers think of avocado oil, we want them to think of Omega Pressery.”
Building a more valuable and sustainable avocado supply chain
Omega Pressery works with thousands of smallholder farmers across East Africa, the majority of whom are women, including in Kenya and Uganda, with Tanzania next in its expansion plans.
Working with its pressing partners, the business turned more than 4 million Grade B avocados into oil last year, creating value from fruit that might otherwise have limited commercial value. It pays above-market rates to encourage harvesting when fruit is ready, while by-products are repurposed for uses including animal feed, manure and biofuel briquettes.
Direct relationships with growers, selected pressing facilities close to growing regions and a local team of agronomy, procurement and sourcing specialists help Omega Pressery develop a more traceable and resilient supply chain as it scales.

items.title: FTSE 100 landowner pulls £1.5bn London shopping centre plans in row with Green council
items.summary: A FTSE 100-listed landowner has shelved plans for a £1.5bn shopping centre project in South London after a local Green-run council refused to co-operate with the plans. Property giant Landsec, which owns Lewisham Shopping Centre, said it is “deprioritising” its plans to redevelop the site following a row with the local authority over affordable housing.  [...]
items.body:
FTSE 100 landowner pulls £1.5bn London shopping centre plans in row with Green council
A FTSE 100-listed landowner has shelved plans for a £1.5bn shopping centre project in South London after a local Green-run council refused to co-operate with the plans.
Property giant Landsec, which owns Lewisham Shopping Centre, said it is “deprioritising” its plans to redevelop the site following a row with the local authority over affordable housing.
Lewisham Shopping Centre will join a growing list of stalled regeneration projects in London, as developers warn that rising costs and local opposition are making building in the capital unviable.
Landsec’s plans to build 1,744 flats, student accommodation and a new shopping centre on the 17-acre site were approved by Lewisham Council in October last year.
This decision gave the landowner permission to demolish the existing mall, which has stood since 1977, to make way for tower blocks up to 35 storeys high.
But the project had recently been engulfed by a row over social housing, after it emerged that Landsec would only be able to make 98 homes available for social rent, with another 231 allocated for discount rates or for social workers.
Landsec said it had decided to shelve the project after the Green-run council refused to exercise compulsory purchase powers to speed up delivery of the site unless Landsec offered to provide more affordable housing.
Building becomes ‘increasingly challenging’
The property giant said: “Recent statements from Lewisham Council also make clear that the administration is not able to support the next phase of land assembly needed to unlock delivery without a significant increase in affordable housing.
“This would require material changes to the masterplan resulting in substantial delays to the programme.”
Landsec said it is “no secret” that higher interest rates, rising construction costs and complex red tape are tying the hands of London’s builders, making big projects “increasingly challenging”.
“This position, combined with the exceptionally challenging economic conditions, mean that we no longer see a sufficiently certain route to delivery and have taken the difficult decision to de-prioritise the redevelopment of Lewisham Shopping Centre to focus on other residential projects,” the firm added.
Landsec’s decision to stall the project was welcomed by some campaign groups, including the Lewisham People’s Assembly, who claimed the redevelopment would have caused “mass displacement”.
Liam Shrivavasta, the Green Party mayor of Lewisham, said: “I know there were many people who were concerned about this development and will welcome this news. I also know there were many other residents who were looking forward to work starting next year.
“The fact is the conditions for such developments are simply not favourable right now.”
Earlier this month, housebuilder Taylor Wimpey said the case for major projects in London has “evaporated” because of onerous red tape and planning objections.
Berkeley, another leading housebuilder, has recently hit out at decisions to block its developments in Peckham and Kingston upon Thames.
Rob Perrins, the firm’s executive chair, said there is a “gulf between positive planning policies and what actually happens when you try to build homes in London. All the policies support housing, but the decisions block it time and time again”.

items.body:
France’s best kept secret, Marie Morin chocolate mousse, lands in 300 M&S stores and has French expats and influencers going wild: “It’s one of the first things I buy when I go home to Paris”.
Forget elaborate dinner-party desserts and hours spent in the kitchen, one of France’s best-loved chocolate mousses has newly arrived in Britain and influencers are already declaring it their new favourite sweet treat.
Marie Morin’s iconic Traditional Chocolate Mousse is now available in 300 Marks & Spencer stores across the UK, giving British shoppers the chance to try the French dessert that has been a firm favourite across the Channel for years. And if the reaction on social media is anything to go by, it could be the latest French food import to cause a stir.
One influencer described the mousse as “quite possibly one of the nicest things I’ve ever had in my mouth… WOW!!”, while another simply called it “my new favourite chocolate mousse.”
For French expat and foodie @frenchfamilyfood, the arrival has been particularly exciting, admitting that the mousse is “one of the first things I buy when I go home to Paris” and saying she was “so thrilled that it’s now available to buy in the UK.”
Meanwhile, @charlottecohencooks praised the indulgent dessert, highlighting its nutritional credentials saying: “These Marie Morin Dark Chocolate mousses are SO good. Also 8g protein per pot?! Don’t mind if I do.”
And it is not just the taste getting attention. Food influencer @frenchfoodielover was won over by the mousse’s glossy appearance, texture and intense chocolate flavour, describing its “shiny finish” as “incredible” and praising its “really intense chocolate taste.”
So, what is all the fuss about? Unlike many supermarket desserts, Marie Morin’s Traditional Chocolate Mousse is made with just three ingredients: pure cocoa butter chocolate, free-range eggs and salted butter. Made in Brittany and served in distinctive glass jars, it has a rich chocolate flavour and smooth, airy texture, with no colouring agents or preservatives. And it seems Brits are increasingly happy to spend a little more on a quality chocolate treat. Recent Mintel research found that 61% of chocolate lovers see premium chocolate as an “affordable luxury”, with shoppers increasingly favouring quality over quantity[1].
David Morin, who leads UK development for Marie Morin, said “Our family has always believed that the best desserts are made with simple, high-quality ingredients and recipes that stay true to tradition. Expanding beyond France has long been an ambition for us, and launching in the UK is an exciting milestone. To secure a listing with Marks & Spencer from the outset is phenomenal. We are delighted that British shoppers can now discover a dessert that has been loved in France for generations.”
With French food continuing to inspire British shoppers, Marie Morin’s arrival could prove to be the latest Gallic import to make the leap from French favourite to British fridge staple. And judging by the early reaction from influencers, the French really may have been keeping this chocolate mousse to themselves for far too long!
Marie Morin Traditional Chocolate Mousse (2 x 100g) is available in selected 300 Marks & Spencer stores across the UK, RRP £4.79.

items.title: Sharps launches new retail concept with Rugby store opening
items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more. Sharps has opened a new concept store at Elliott’s Field Shopping Park in Rugby as part of a wider programme of investment in its retail estate, with further locations set to follow. The 3412 sq ft store represents a substantial investment from the company, showcasing several room settings above and beyond the core bedroom offering […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Sharps has opened a new concept store at Elliott’s Field Shopping Park in Rugby as part of a wider programme of investment in its retail estate, with further locations set to follow.
The 3412 sq ft store represents a substantial investment from the company, showcasing several room settings above and beyond the core bedroom offering that Sharps has been known for. The opening of the store has provided an additional four jobs for the local economy, and plans are afoot that if the new concept store model is successful, a plan will be developed to roll out further stores across the country.
The new format has been developed to strengthen the role of physical retail within Sharps’ wider sales and design model, creating a larger, more design-led environment in which customers can begin planning their space before progressing to the brand’s established in-home design consultation service.
Located alongside other home, furniture and lifestyle retailers at Elliott’s Field, the Rugby store also reflects a deliberate move towards destination retail. The larger footprint gives Sharps greater visibility among customers already shopping for the home, while providing the space needed to showcase its new design services as well as a broader range of fitted solutions beyond the bedroom.
Rather than replacing Sharps’ existing model, where sales and design experts visit customers at home to understand the space, take measurements and develop a tailored solution, the store adds an earlier stage to the journey.
Customers can explore full room schemes, finishes and materials, work through initial ideas with the store’s Studio Designers and create moodboards before those ideas are developed further within their own home.
The format enables Sharps to showcase multiple room solutions within one location, supporting the company’s expansion into spaces including home offices, living areas, boot rooms and other parts of the home where fitted furniture can provide both storage and design benefits.
Paul McClenaghan, CEO of Sharps Furniture Group, said: “Our investment in Rugby is about defining what we need from physical retail as the customer journey continues to evolve.
“The showroom is no longer the only place where people begin researching a purchase, but that does not make the physical environment less important. It means it has to work harder. Customers need to be able to experience the quality of the product, explore different solutions and get meaningful design input when they visit.
“We have a very strong in-home sales and design model and that remains fundamental to the business. What this format allows us to do is strengthen the journey around it. A customer can begin thinking through their space, their style and what they need from it in store, and our experts can then take that thinking into the home and develop a solution around the realities of the individual property.
“The larger footprint also gives us an opportunity to demonstrate the breadth of what Sharps can now offer. We want customers to see us as a fitted furniture business for the whole home, and being able to show those different applications together is an important part of that.
“Rugby gives us a format from which we can learn as we continue to invest in our estate. It is about creating stores that have a clear role within the wider business and making physical retail work harder at every stage of the customer journey.”
The opening forms part of Sharps’ wider retail investment programme, with several further locations planned to follow as the business develops the concept across its estate.
The Sharps Rugby concept store is located at Elliott’s Field Shopping Park, Leicester Road, Rugby, CV21 1SR.

items.title: Toby Carvery’s new frozen range wins over UK consumers, System1 finds

Toby Carvery’s move into the frozen food aisle looks set to be a hit with UK consumers, according to new testing from market research company System1 Group. The restaurant chain’s new 15-product frozen range, which has launched exclusively at Iceland and The Food Warehouse, achieved a strong 4.2-Star rating on System1’s Test Your Innovation. The […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Toby Carvery’s move into the frozen food aisle looks set to be a hit with UK consumers, according to new testing from market research company System1 Group.
The restaurant chain’s new 15-product frozen range, which has launched exclusively at Iceland and The Food Warehouse, achieved a strong 4.2-Star rating on System1’s Test Your Innovation. The Star rating measure consumers’ emotional responses and predicts the sales success of new innovations.
The range also achieved a Buy Shares score of 72%, meaning nearly three-quarters of respondents said they would buy shares in the idea. The score places the range among the top 15% of comparable innovations in System1’s database of more than 60,000 tested ideas.
The range also received an Emotion-into-Action™ score of 77, classified as ‘Good’. This metric combines the type and intensity of consumers’ emotional responses, giving greater weight to emotions most likely to translate into action.
Almost two-thirds (63%) of consumers expressed a positive emotional response, comprising happiness (52%) and surprise (11%). By contrast, just 6% expressed negative emotions. Convenience and variety in particular emerged as spontaneous drivers of happiness, with consumers welcoming the opportunity to enjoy Toby Carvery favourites at home and the breadth of dishes available.
The concept also demonstrated strong brand alignment, with 92% of respondents agreeing that it fitted with the Toby Carvery brand, while 94% considered the range recognisable.
The findings come as restaurant brands increasingly look beyond their traditional dining locations to establish a presence in UK supermarkets. Brands including Pizza Express, Nando’s and Itsu have already expanded into retail, tapping into consumer demand for familiar restaurant experiences at home.
Tristan Findlay, chief growth officer – innovation at System1, commented: “Toby Carvery has done the unexpected, bringing the Sunday roast straight into people’s homes with a ready-to-eat range. It may not be one for me personally, but I’m clearly not speaking for UK consumers, who rated it a strong 4.2 Stars, a sign it’s set to drive trial.
“Hats off to the team: it’s a move nobody saw coming, and the timing is spot on, with hearty British comfort food landing just as the colder months set in. Whether shoppers stick with the freezer aisle or head back to their local carvery will come down to product quality, but in the short term, this one is set to sell.”

items.body:
Asda has today launched Asda Roots – a new apprenticeship programme that gives young people not currently in work or education a permanent job, combined with training and a recognised qualification.
The Asda Roots programme will initially welcome 16 young people into roles across 8 stores, with plans to take on 250 more recruits in 2027. The programme combines permanent paid employment with structured on-the-job learning, allowing participants to earn while they work towards a nationally recognised Level 2 qualification, equivalent to five GCSEs.
Aimed at 18 to 21-year-olds who are not currently in employment, education or training (NEET), Asda Roots will be delivered through the Government’s flagship Foundation Apprenticeship programme and has been developed in partnership with the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) and Inspiro Learning.
The programme forms part of Asda’s wider commitment to creating opportunities for young people and helping more people access meaningful, long-term employment.
James Goodman, chief people officer at Asda, said: ” Too many young people are held back because they haven’t had the opportunity to gain the skills and experience employers look for. Asda Roots aims to break that cycle by combining a permanent job with training, mentoring and a recognised qualification.
We want to give young people the opportunity to earn, learn and develop the skills they need to succeed. Many retail leaders started their careers on the shop floor, and we’re excited to help the next generation take their first step with Asda.”
Minister for Skills, Baroness Jacqui Smith said: “Too often, young people’s futures are shaped by circumstances beyond their control, and we are determined to change that.
“It’s brilliant to see Asda providing new opportunities for young people out of work and education and helping them kickstart their career.
“It comes alongside our reforms to deliver 50,000 more apprenticeships for young people because everyone deserves the chance to earn, learn and build a career, no matter where they start.”
The pilot gave young people referred by the DWP the opportunity to gain valuable workplace experience and take part in a guaranteed interview. Candidates who were not selected for Asda Roots were also considered for seasonal roles where suitable vacancies were available.
Those who demonstrate strong potential will also have opportunities to continue their development through further apprenticeships and career progression across the business.
In addition to workplace experience, apprentices will receive dedicated mentoring, financial literacy training and practical life skills support designed to help them thrive both in and outside of work.
Asda currently supports around 600 apprentices across its business and plans for Asda Roots to become an important pathway for attracting and developing the next generation of retail talent.
The launch builds on Asda’s wider commitment to helping more young people into work. Last month, the retailer announced a significant expansion of its supported internship programme in partnership with DFN Project SEARCH, creating opportunities for more than 200 young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) across 35 stores.

items.title: ACS calls on government to support hard-hit forecourts
items.summary: The Association of Convenience Stores (ACS) has called on the chancellor to act in the Budget to support the UK's 8,300+ petrol forecourts, who have been hit hard by higher costs and extremely challenging sales conditions made worse by skyrocketing pump prices. ACS' 2026 Forecourt… This story continues at ACS calls on government to support hard-hit forecourts Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
ACS’ 2026 Forecourt Report has revealed that UK forecourts have less room to invest than last year, with each store spending £14,810 on average compared to £15,550 in 2025.
ACS has warned that investment is being constrained because of major increases in business rates bills for forecourt retailers and the pressure of continued rises in employment costs.
At the till, customer spending is taking a hit due to the sharp rise in fuel prices over the last year, with an average spend of £13.09 compared to £13.48 in 2025 (excluding fuel).
ACS chief executive Ed Woodall said: “It’s easy for the government to point the finger at forecourts when fuel prices go up, but the reality is that they’re exposed to pump price rises themselves.
“When prices at the pump increase, forecourt retailers are losing out because, customers don’t spend as much in store and they rely on those sales to trade viably.”
“Forecourts are crucial national infrastructure and incredibly important to the communities they serve, but have been disproportionately hit by business rates increases, new regulatory reporting requirements and other cost of trading pressures.
“We are calling on the chancellor to take action in the Budget to support both customers and forecourt retailers by freezing fuel duty beyond January 2027, help them to invest by taking pressure off rates bills, and recognise the role they play in providing secure local jobs to over 90,000 people.”
Additional key findings from the Forecourt Report include:
- Forecourts are rated by consumers as one of the top five most essential services in the local community
- 77% of forecourt retailers engaged in some form of community activity over the last year
- 40% of forecourt retailers are now aged 30 or under
- 21% of forecourt retailers took no time off last year
ACS’ #Checkout the Cost of Trading campaign has been running throughout the summer, highlighting the pressure that the convenience sector is under and calling on the government to act. More information on the Cost of Trading campaign hub is here:

items.body:
Getty Images/Maskot
Capita postpones investor event to focus on CSPS fix
Capita has pulled the plug on a planned event for investors, financial analysts and shareholders to prioritise addressing Civil Service Pension Scheme issues
Capita cannot hold an event for shareholders, investors and market watchers because it wants to focus on fixing the botched administration of the Civil Service Pension Scheme (CSPS).
The troubled scheme has already reduced the firm’s profits by £40m.
The outsourcer said its Capital Market Event, planned for 4 November, had been postponed to enable it to “focus on improving the service delivery on the Civil Service Pension Scheme contract”.
It said it will include an update when it announces its trading statement next month. “Alongside its regular trading update in December, Capita will provide a comprehensive update, including detail on the group’s new operational segments following completion of the disposal of the private sector contact centre business,” said a company statement.
It added that it is making good operational progress with the CSPS contract. “This includes the roll-out of new features and further planned upgrades, such as the launch of the retirement modelling tool, which is due to go live in the coming weeks,” it said.
“Capita recognises further improvement in service is required, and we are implementing further automation and strengthening governance, including improved management information.”
Alongside the Cabinet Office, it said it is working on a comprehensive recovery plan, “focusing on improving member experience and delivering operational stability”.
Pension disaster
In 2023, the Cabinet Office awarded Capita a seven-year contract worth £239m for the administration of the CSPS, which has 1.7 million members. The takeover from the previous administrator, MyCSP, took place on 1 December 2025.
Since it took on the contract, Capita has failed to meet its delivery promises, leaving claimants in severe financial difficulties. Thousands of retired civil servants are affected by the CSPS problems – some have waited nearly a year for their pensions, and at least one has been forced to use a food bank.
Capita has admitted it is set to lose money on the contract, with pressure mounting on the organisation, which is heavily reliant on public sector business, due to the government’s current insourcing plans combined with its much-publicised failures.
In January 2026, just a month after Capita took over from MyCSP and following a litany of problems, a troubleshooter stepped in from HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) to lead an “urgent recovery plan”, which included 150 staff being moved temporarily from HMRC to the service.
Disaster after disaster has now prompted the government to make the decision to bring the service in-house, but no timeline has been given.
A Cabinet Office spokesperson recently told Computer Weekly that the government is “actively shaping a long-term strategy to bring the pension scheme back in-house” – a statement repeated by Cabinet Office minister Sally Jameson.
What is now clear is that the government won’t let Capita flee without fixing a scheme it will inevitably lose. In the debate, Jameson declared her support for the government’s plan for the biggest wave of insourcing in a generation, but made clear that Capita cannot just walk away, leaving a mess.
“I want Capita to pay for their mistakes, not the taxpayers to pay for their mistakes. They don’t get to just walk away and do nothing about it,” she told MPs. “They need to pay for this, they need to get everyone their pensions, and then we’ll look at what needs to be done in terms of the viability of the scheme long term.”
Civil servant campaign groups are demanding the scheme is fixed before the government makes a decision about its future.

items.body:
Ikea stumps up £31.5 million as it looks to make UK fulfilment more efficient and reduce packaging waste
Ikea UK is investing £31.5 million across its Peterborough and Doncaster customer distribution centres (CDC) as the retailer aims to make online fulfilment more efficient and sustainable. In Peterborough, new technology is packaging customer orders to size and reducing material usage by up to 30%, by preventing waste from oversized boxes and filling paper. In Doncaster, Ikea is trialling a new regional fulfilment capability, serving customers in the north and Scotland from a closer location to them.
The investments will strengthen Ikea’s UK fulfilment network as online sales account for 43.3% of total UK sales in financial year 2026. It is investing £30 million in new technology for its Peterborough CDC, with the upgrades taking place over a two-year period. As part of this, it has launched new PackSize technology to prevent waste from oversized cardboard boxes and filling materials by packaging customer orders to size. On average, the technology reduces material usage by up to 30% and void fill by up to 60%.
The technology is expected to increase the share of parcels processed through automation at the Peterborough CDC from 47% today to 75% in 2027, helping the fulfilment team prepare orders for delivery more efficiently. These additional orders would otherwise have been packaged by manually creating a packing carton which includes having to measure the article then creating the cartons to fit the order. Three drones and nests were introduced at the site in January to support inventory management. They scan each aisle in short cycles, helping Ikea to keep stock in the right place and meet customer demand.
Ikea is investing £1.5 million in trialling a new fulfilment capability at its Doncaster CDC. The site now fulfils orders for customers in the Gateshead, Edinburgh and Glasgow areas, with plans for Sheffield to follow. By fulfilling these orders from Doncaster rather than Peterborough, Ikea expects to reduce emissions from delivery journeys by an estimated 280 tonnes of CO2 annually. The new capability has created an additional 80 jobs at the Doncaster site.
David McCabe, CEO and CSO at Ikea UK&IE, says: “We are always on the lookout for new ways to do things better, and that’s true across the operational side of our business just as much as the innovative new products and services we bring to market. These investments in our Peterborough and Doncaster CDCs will ensure fulfilment is smoother than ever and reduce our environmental footprint, while positioning the business for long-term success by strengthening operational efficiency and supporting sustainable growth.”
“Our wonderful teams of co-workers in Peterborough and Doncaster work tirelessly getting orders to our customers, and we couldn’t function without them. We’re empowering our people to get the best out of these new technologies, and we’re excited to watch them grow alongside the business.”

items.body:
Co-op and Devon & Cornwall Police double retail crime cases solved with new reporting system roll-out
The number of retail crime cases solved has almost doubled during a new crime reporting trial between Co-op and Devon and Cornwall Police in the UK. The partnership, according to those involved, delivers significantly faster justice for offences carried out, with data from Devon & Cornwall Police showing crimes reported through the platform - which is called SentrySIS - achieving a solve rate of almost 60%, which is approaching double the force’s average solve rate for retail crime versus retail crime being reported by those using traditional channels.
Data from Devon & Cornwall Police also revealed that 90% of identified shop theft offenders are repeat offenders, with just 50 individuals responsible for around a quarter of all shop theft offences in the Devon and Cornwall force area, often with more than 100 known offences each. The new system enables stronger intelligence sharing; improved tracking of repeat offenders - connecting multiple offences committed by the same individual and building stronger cases against prolific offenders and, closer collaboration with police both at a local and central level.
Store colleagues upload incident details, CCTV, photos and impact statement enabling police to record and allocate the crime in as little 30 minutes - a process that could take police up to seven days. Furthermore, it removes the need for investigating officers to then approach the retailer for evidence, saving time for retailers and resulting in the average time taken for investigations to be completed and assigned an outcome being slashed by more than a third to 35 days.
The success of the pilot has seen the SentrySIS system, which links to Co-op’s wider partnership working with UK Partners Against Crime (UKPAC), now activated across all Co-op stores in Devon and Cornwall, with discussions now underway with additional police forces. Co-op’s own retail crime levels are falling with the retailer expected to see its lowest levels since the pandemic.
Overall retail crime at Co-op is down almost 20% year-on-year, with incidents of anti-social behaviour and verbal abuse reducing by 35%, along with a double-digit drop in physical assaults. At the same time, however, it remains cautiously optimistic as retail crime levels remain double those levels seen pre-pandemic after the shop crime surge at the start of the decade.
Paul Gerrard, Director - Campaigns, Public Affairs and Policy, Co-op, says: “The reduction in retail crime at Co-op is very welcome, but these are green shoots with crime levels remaining higher than before the pandemic. The success of this initiative demonstrates the benefits that we know can be realised when retailers and police work together. We have seen that offenders can be identified and investigations can progress much faster and, importantly for everyone, outcomes improve significantly. The fact that such a high proportion of crimes are carried out by repeat and prolific offenders highlights why early intervention is so important - every successful investigation has the potential to prevent many future offences from blighting our high streets and local communities.”
Chris Chaloner, Business Crime Sergeant for Devon & Cornwall Police, says: "The results from this pilot have been extremely impressive. The evidence provided through the platform is available to officers immediately, allowing investigations to progress much more quickly. Crucially, this approach helps us to link crimes and identify and target those prolific offenders who are responsible for a disproportionate amount of retail crime. We know that a relatively small number of individuals commit a large volume of offences. By working closely with retailers, building effective partnership and receiving high-quality evidence we can take earlier action, secure more charges and achieve better outcomes for our high streets and communities."
Policing Minister, Sarah Jones, comments: “Collaboration between the retail industry, police and government is exactly what I want to see as Chair of the Retail Crime Forum. This pilot is a great example of what can be achieved when working together to tackle crime. Shop theft is falling across the country, and more criminals are being charged. This is good progress, but we will go further, restoring neighbourhood policing, with thousands more officers already in our communities. We are also changing the law to make it clearer that there will be consequences for shop theft of any value and bringing in a standalone offence for assaulting a retail worker.”
Alastair Woodburn, a Co-op Store Manager in Exeter, says: "The system has fundamentally changed the way we report crime. Our store was one of the first to adopt it. It is quicker to use and gives us confidence that the information police officers need is available to them immediately - and the outcomes are fantastic. Retail crime can be challenging on the frontline, but it is a rewarding job too.”
'“The majority of people rely on and value a local community shop, unfortunately it is just a small number of offenders carrying out most of the crime. This process Identifies and links offenders - building the full picture. Co-op has invested significantly in safety and security measures, and this latest measure sends a loud message to offenders, it clearly shows just how effective it can be when retailers and police work together to tackle the prolific offenders that do so much harm in communities."

items.body:
British bicycle brand Brompton backs BigCommerce as new portal replaces 12-year-old wholesale system
Commerce reports that Brompton, a British foldable bicycle manufacturer, has launched its new partner portal on BigCommerce B2B Edition.
The aim here is to give Brompton’s global network of independent retailers a modern ordering experience, with the portal running on the same BigCommerce instance and product catalogue that powers the company’s direct-to-consumer business.
Brompton first launched its composable direct-to-consumer site on BigCommerce in 2024. The new offering extends that foundation to the wholesale side of the business, which accounts for roughly 75% of Brompton’s total sales across over 1,000 retail partners worldwide.
“Our retail partners are central to Brompton's success. The new Partner Portal gives them a modern, intuitive way to explore our product range, place orders and access the information they need to support our joint customers.” says Oliver Boardman, CTO at Brompton. “This investment is about making it easier for our partners to do business with Brompton and grow alongside us.”
The previous wholesale system was created more than a decade ago and was designed around the company's configurable bicycles. As its range expanded to include electric, titanium and large wheel bikes, the breadth of products, options and content available to partners grew significantly. The new portal provides, according to a press release, “a richer product experience, with clearer imagery, improved product information and curated catalogues that make it easier for partners to understand and access the full Brompton range, while also providing a more scalable foundation for future growth.”
Over time, Brompton plans to increase the range of tools it provides in the system.
“This wasn't just a technology project. It was delivered through close collaboration between teams across Brompton, combining deep knowledge of our products, partners and processes with the technical expertise to bring it all together. AI tools helped accelerate delivery, but the real success came from having engaged people across the business working towards a shared goal,” says Boardman. “That collaboration, combined with the knowledge we've built on the BigCommerce platform, allowed us to launch significantly faster while continuing to build our internal capabilities.”
The portal is live in Germany and Austria, with the remaining European markets and the UK to follow this month. Additional localisation work for the U., Japan, China and Singapore is underway, with full roll-out targeted for completion ahead of the spring.
“Historically we had different systems for different things,” says Boardman. “We want to bring it all together so there’s a single place partners can come to interact with the brand. If we make it as easy as possible for people to work with us, that helps them give our customers a great experience.”
"For years, manufacturers put their digital investment into direct-to-consumer while their dealers made do with ordering tools no shopper would tolerate," says Lance Owide, Vice President of B2B Product Management at Commerce. "That gap is common across manufacturing, but it's closing fast. Brompton deserves credit for recognising the need to serve consumers and partners from one platform, one catalog and one team.”

Quail Digital bags a place among Technology Vendor of the Year (UK) finalsts at RTIH Innovation Awards
Retail communications specialist Quail Digital has been named a finalist in the Technology Vendor of the Year (UK) category at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards which celebrate innovation and excellence across the retail technology sector.
The category recognises companies developing innovative technologies that help retailers transform customer experience, improve back-end operations or achieve both.
Quail Digital’s new Pro12 retail headset system incorporates speech recognition and can integrate with AI and connected retail systems which can allow employees to ask questions by voice and receive information through their headsets. This includes checking stock availability without leaving the shop floor to find a colleague or use another device.
The development reflects a wider challenge for retailers as store technology becomes more sophisticated - ensuring that employees can access the information it generates without adding complexity to their working day.
More than 3,000 Quail Digital Pro12 headsets are now in use across more than 500 SPAR stores in the UK and Ireland, demonstrating the technology’s practical application in busy retail environments. The scale of the deployment has also led to the company being appointed as a preferred supplier to SPAR International.
The headsets can also be used to communicate emergency alerts, allowing colleagues to notify one another when assistance is required. This is particularly relevant in convenience retail, where employees may have to manage customer service and security concerns simultaneously.
Tom Downes, CEO at Quail Digital, says: “We’re pleased to be recognised by the RTIH Innovation Awards. As more technology is introduced into stores, retailers also need to consider how employees interact with it. Giving frontline teams easier access to information, without taking them away from customers or adding extra steps to their work, will be an important part of making connected retail systems useful in practice.”

Live commerce specialist Whatnot is doubling Irish workforce as It opens doors to new Dublin office
Whatnot, a live commerce platform operating in North America, the UK and Europe, has opened its new European headquarters in Dublin, announcing plans to double its Irish workforce over the next 18 months and open its platform to Irish small businesses in 2027. The company currently employs more than 130 people across the country and is hiring across engineering and AI, operations, strategy, and trust and safety.
“The depth of engineering and AI talent coming out of Ireland’s universities is a big part of why we keep growing the team here,” says Grant LaFontaine, Co-founder and CEO at Whatnot. “Sellers around the world rely on what our Dublin engineers build every day to grow their businesses, and there’s a lot more to build. We’re also opening the platform to small businesses in Ireland next year, so local shops and entrepreneurs can reach the people already shopping on Whatnot in Ireland and around the world, who will then be able to discover the creativity and talent of Irish businesses and entrepreneurs.”
Minister of State Alan Dillon, Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment says: “I warmly welcome Whatnot’s decision to establish its new European headquarters in Dublin and to significantly expand its Irish workforce over the coming months. The company’s plan to double its team in Ireland, creating high-quality jobs across engineering, AI, operations, and trust and safety, is a strong endorsement of the exceptional talent available here and of Ireland’s attractiveness as a location for innovation. I wish the Whatnot team every success as they grow their presence in Ireland’s thriving tech ecosystem.”
Mary Buckley, Executive Director at IDA Ireland comments: “Whatnot’s decision to expand its Dublin team demonstrates strong confidence in Ireland’s technology ecosystem and skilled workforce. The new roles in engineering, AI, trust and risk and customer experience highlights the strategic activity being undertaken in Ireland and supports our strategy to attract investments in innovation and digital technologies. IDA Ireland is delighted to partner with Whatnot in this next stage of growth.”

SPAR International and Footprints AI come together to increase consumer connections via new platform
Footprints AI and SPAR International have announced a partnership to develop a media marketplace that supports independently operated food retail. The platform would be available to all SPAR licensees, enabling SPAR country organisations to access a single platform to plan, buy, optimise, and measure retail media campaigns, with the same simplicity, precision, and sales tracking as digital advertising.
Footprints AI’s software sits on top of SPAR country organisations’ existing physical and digital retail infrastructure (stores, screens, instore radio, e-commerce, mobile apps, and PoS data) and connects it into one advertiser facing marketplace, while ensuring each organisation keeps full control of its own data, assets, and commercial model.
“Retail media has reached a point where brands and agencies no longer need an isolated network. They need a marketplace that can scale outcomes. The first phase of retail media was about individual retailers monetising their own assets. The next phase is global marketplace infrastructure: advertisers get a more consistent way to plan, buy, optimise, and measure retail media across markets, while local retailers keep control of their data, assets, and commercial model. That is the shift we are building with SPAR,” says Dan Marc, CEO, Footprints AI.
“Retail media is an important growth platform in modern retail. At SPAR our ambition is to connect the strength of our global SPAR network with the power of local retail entrepreneurship, creating a scalable platform that delivers value for customers, retailers and brand partners alike. By combining our vast physical presence, shopper relationships and data capabilities with advanced retail media technology, we are evolving our network into a connected commercial ecosystem that enables brands to engage consumers more effectively across markets while generating new revenue opportunities for SPAR country organisations,” says Tobias Wasmuht, CEO, SPAR International.

items.title: Warehouse tax ‘dropped over fears of Trump trade war’
items.summary: Andy Burnham’s plans for a so-called ‘warehouse tax’ were dropped over fears a raid on US firms like Amazon could spark a trade war with Donald Trump, a top industry body has claimed. The Prime Minister, during his campaign to become Makerfield MP, pledged to hike business rates on “out of town” warehouses to fund [...]
items.body:
Warehouse tax ‘dropped over fears of Trump trade war’
Andy Burnham’s plans for a so-called ‘warehouse tax’ were dropped over fears a raid on US firms like Amazon could spark a trade war with Donald Trump, a top industry body has claimed.
The Prime Minister, during his campaign to become Makerfield MP, pledged to hike business rates on “out of town” warehouses to fund cuts for high street shops, but the Chancellor has since ruled out the plans.
The boss of a top hospitality industry body has now claimed ministers backed down on the plans over fears it could trigger the ire of US President Donald Trump.
Allen Simpson, chief executive of UKHospitality, told City AM: “We have been told the problem is that the big online giants are American, and the White House will look very badly on any tax rise, which hits, say, Amazon.
“That’s not contested. That’s just what the officials say. The problem is: we can’t fix business rates without taxing the big American online giants, and we don’t want to do that because it will start a trade war with Trump.”
The hospitality industry has been attempting to convince the government that high street businesses like pubs pay an unfair share of business rates, compared to online giants like Amazon and Ebay.
Though business rates are currently based on the value of a company’s property, Simpson claims the system should be reformed to, for example, determine a firm’s bill as a percentage of its revenue.
“The problem is that if you make it a percentage of revenue, so [that] an Amazon warehouse is paying as much as a hotel, you have to dramatically increase the business rates on Amazon warehouses,” he said.
Retail bosses against warehouse tax
Simpson said he had been told by officials in Keir Starmer’s governments that they were avoiding a warehouse tax to dodge a trade war with Trump, adding that he believes Healey’s decision to rule out the tax was based on the same calculation.
A Treasury spokesperson said: “As has always been the case, decisions on tax are a matter for the Chancellor to set out at fiscal events, and we do not routinely comment on rumour, speculation or proposals.”
The US President has threatened a trade war in response to UK tax hikes in the past, when he vowed to impose 100 per cent tariffs in response to a digital services tax on American tech firms.
A potential warehouse tax had been staunchly opposed by retail bosses. They claimed that the measure would push up tax on sites used by retailers for storage and distribution, inevitably forcing price rises for shoppers.
Jason Tarry, the chair of John Lewis and Waitrose, had said the tax raid would “reveal a fundamental misunderstanding of how modern high streets work”.
The government says it is taking other measures to support hospitality firms. In July, Burnham announced a 20 per cent business rates cut for pubs.
Speaking at a UKHospitality event on Tuesday, business minister Kate Dearden told sector bosses the government will help deliver “more investment, more jobs, more opportunities, and stronger high streets, and the sustainable growth that reaches every single part of this country”.

items.title: Co-op and police double retail crime cases solved with new system
items.summary: New data has revealed that the number of retail crime cases solved has almost doubled during a new crime reporting trial between Co-op and Devon and Cornwall Police. Data from Devon & Cornwall Police show crimes reported through the platform - which is called SentrySIS… This story continues at Co-op and police double retail crime cases solved with new system Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Data from Devon & Cornwall Police show crimes reported through the platform – which is called SentrySIS – is achieving a solve rate of almost 60%, approaching double the force’s average solve rate for shop theft reported through traditional channels.
New data also revealed that 90% of identified shop theft offenders are repeat offenders, with just 50 individuals responsible for around a quarter of all shop theft offences in the Devon and Cornwall force area, often with more than 100 known offences each – highlighting the benefits of early intervention to prevent further offences blighting local communities.
The new system enables stronger intelligence sharing; improved tracking of repeat offenders – connecting multiple offences committed by the same individual and building stronger cases against prolific offenders and, closer collaboration with police both at a local and central level.
Store colleagues upload incident details, CCTV, photos and impact statement enabling police to record and allocate the crime in as little 30 minutes – a process that could take police up to seven days.
Furthermore, it removes the need for investigating officers to then approach the retailer for evidence, saving time for retailers and resulting in the average time taken for investigations to be completed and assigned an outcome being slashed by more than a third to just 35 days.
The success of the pilot has seen the SentrySIS system – which links to Co-op’s wider partnership working with UK Partners Against Crime (UKPAC) – activated across all Co-op stores in Devon and Cornwall, with discussions now underway with additional police forces.
Co-op’s own retail crime levels are falling with the retailer expected to see its lowest levels since the pandemic.
The retailer has long been at the forefront of turning a spotlight on the organised criminality blighting communities.
Overall retail crime at Co-op is down almost 20% year-on-year, incidents of anti-social behaviour and verbal abuse reducing by more than a third (35%), along with a double-digit drop in physical assaults.
However, Co-op said it remains cautiously optimistic as retail crime levels remain double those levels seen pre-pandemic after the shop crime surge at the start of the decade.
It added that continued co-operation amongst retailers, police and government is needed to bring about meaningful, sustained and lasting change to tackling retail crime, and its underlying causes.
Paul Gerrard, director – campaigns, public affairs and policy, Co-op, said: “The reduction in retail crime at Co-op is very welcome, but these are green shoots with crime levels remaining higher than before the pandemic.
“The success of this initiative demonstrates the benefits that we know can be realised when retailers and police work together. We have seen that offenders can be identified and investigations can progress much faster and, importantly for everyone, outcomes improve significantly.
“The fact that such a high proportion of crimes are carried out by repeat and prolific offenders highlights why early intervention is so important – every successful investigation has the potential to prevent many future offences from blighting our high streets and local communities.”
Chris Chaloner, business crime sergeant for Devon & Cornwall Police, said: “The results from this pilot have been extremely impressive. The evidence provided through the platform is available to officers immediately, allowing investigations to progress much more quickly.
“Crucially, this approach helps us to link crimes and identify and target prolific those offenders who are responsible for a disproportionate amount of retail crime. We know that a relatively small number of individuals commit a large volume of offences.
“By working closely with retailers, building effective partnership and receiving high-quality evidence we can take earlier action, secure more charges and achieve better outcomes for our high streets and communities.”
Alastair Woodburn, a Co-op store manager in Exeter, said: “The system has fundamentally changed the way we report crime. Our store was one of the first to adopt it.
“It is quicker to use and gives us confidence that the information police officers need is available to them immediately – and the outcomes are fantastic, giving the whole team greater confidence that something will happen when we report crime. Retail crime can be challenging on the frontline, but it is a rewarding job too.
“The majority of people rely on and value a local community shop, unfortunately it is just a small number of offenders carrying out most of the crime. This process Identifies and links offenders – building the full picture.
“Co-op has invested significantly in safety and security measures, and this latest measure sends a loud message to offenders, it clearly shows just how effective it can be when retailers and police work together to tackle the prolific offenders that do so much harm in communities.”
Policing minister, Sarah Jones, said: “Collaboration between the retail industry, police and government is exactly what I want to see as Chair of the Retail Crime Forum. This pilot is a great example of what can be achieved when working together to tackle crime.
“Shop theft is falling across the country, and more criminals are being charged. This is good progress, but we will go further, restoring neighbourhood policing, with thousands more officers already in our communities.
“We are also changing the law to make it clearer that there will be consequences for shop theft of any value and bringing in a standalone offence for assaulting a retail worker.”

items.title: Trump tariff fears 'deter Labour from a rates shake-up' that would help hotels but hit online giants like Amazon
items.summary: UK Hospitality said the Government has promised support for hotels in the Budget, after having given a business rates discount to pubs earlier this year.
items.body:
Trump tariff fears 'deter Labour from a rates shake-up' that would help hotels but hit online giants like Amazon
Labour shelved a business rates shake-up that could have helped hotels but hit online giants such as Amazon because of fears of upsetting Donald Trump, it was claimed yesterday.
Industry group UK Hospitality said that Andy Burnham's government has promised support for hotels in the Budget, after giving a business rates discount to pubs earlier this year.
But chairman Allen Simpson told reporters yesterday: 'We've been told consistently by the Treasury and by officials that one of the reasons they're so wary of doing something on business rates is because to pay for it they'll have to put up taxes on Amazon warehouses, and they think that Trump will hit us with a tariff – so that might be technically difficult to do.'
UK Hospitality did not suggest that Amazon had been lobbying the Government against business rate increases or citing the US President in conversations.
A Treasury spokesman said: 'As has always been the case, decisions on tax are a matter for the Chancellor [John Healey] to set out at fiscal events, and we do not routinely comment on rumour, speculation or proposals.'
Simpson said hotels were facing particularly painful conditions after their business rate bills more than doubled over a three-year period.
Industry group UK Hospitality said that Andy Burnham's Government has promised support for hotels in the Budget, after having given a business rates discount to pubs earlier this year
It has been reported that the Government will introduce business rates reductions for small High Street businesses, such as salons and cafes, by lifting 75,000 small properties out of paying rates.
This is to be funded by a tax crackdown on online retailers that will make them responsible for collecting tax from retailers using their marketplaces. The move has been welcomed by Amazon.
But UK Hospitality has urged ministers to extend support to hotels, many of which face the highest business rates multiplier – part of the formula for calculating rates – because they are large properties.
However, Simpson said that a VAT cut – reducing the rate paid by hospitality from 20 per cent to 10 per cent – was 'the single biggest and simplest lever that they could pull'.
He said the Chancellor expressed sympathy for the sector's plight at a recent roundtable meeting with business, agreeing 'that the last few years have been devastating for the High Street, for hospitality in particular'.

items.body:
CAYO, the luxury Irish alpaca knitwear brand, has officially announced its expansion into the UK retail market with a launch at multi-brand boutique destination Square Bath. Located at 12 New Bond St, Bath, BA1 1BE the collection is located on the ground floor next to Isabel Marant, GANNI, rag & bone, Anine Bing and others. CAYO is also now available to shop online in the UK.
Designed in Ireland and knitted by expert craftspeople in Italy, CAYO garments are engineered for year-round versatility. Founded by Limerick designer Orla Daly, CAYO brings a fresh approach to the luxury knitwear sector with seasonless, heirloom-quality pieces. Unlike fast-fashion knits reliant on synthetic blends, CAYO uses zero synthetic plastic fibers, selecting 100% naturally derived, premium Peruvian alpaca wool custom-spun specifically for the brand.
CAYO was born from founder Orla Daly’s passion for slow fashion and self-expression, which began when her parents gifted her a sewing machine at age 15 and was further shaped by her participation in Junk Couture creating garments from 100% recycled materials. After discovering the unique thermal properties and sustainability of alpaca wool during a trip to South America, Daly set out to create a brand built on transparency and longevity. Alpaca farming requires significantly less land and water resources than cashmere goats or mohair rabbits, offering a gentler footprint on the planet.
Square Bath will stock a curated selection of CAYO’s classic collection alongside the brand’s newly released signature button up cardigan in all new colourways. Every CAYO garment features signature structural design choices and distinctive brand accents:
● The Andean Jumper: A neater, structured silhouette featuring a classic relaxed round neck, tailored split hem and long fitted cuffs. Versatile enough to layer over dresses or pair with denim, it offers temperature-regulating comfort suitable for a cool summer evening or a chilly winter day. Available in Nordic Sky Blue, Sunset Pink. Andean Reimagined is available in: Chantilly Cream, Cream and Ink Blue and Cream and Tan Stripe.
● The Classic Jumper: A relaxed-fit pullover designed for effortless everyday layering and soft, draped comfort. Available in Nordic Sky Blue, Deep Navy, Sunset Pink, Muted Animal Print and Tan.
● The Zip Up Hoodie: A relaxed-fit, longer-line zip knit designed for effortless layering. Crafted in versatile shades like Chantilly Cream (accented with a subtle navy cuff stripe), True Tan, Ink Blue and Sunset Pink, it can be styled under a coat for winter or over dresses on cooler summer evenings.
● The Button Up Cardigan: CAYO’s signature silhouette reimagined with fresh colour mixes and bespoke buttons. Features cloud-like softness and the signature coloured stripe on the right cuff. Available in Burnt Orange and Vibrant Green. The Button Up Cardigan Reimagined is available in Tan with Cream Lapel, Chantilly Cream, True Tan and Cream with Tan Lapel.
● Hats & Scarves: Essential luxury cold weather accessories including The Wrap Around Scarf, an indulgent, oversized knit designed for versatile draped styling and The Peak Hat, crafted with generous depth and shape. Both accessory lines feature CAYO’s distinctive signature contrast stripe along the edge and hem. Hats available in Sunset Pink, Chantilly Cream and Tan. Scarves available in Cream and Tan.
● Signature Detail: Every CAYO piece features the brand’s distinct signature detail: a contrast coloured stripe located on the right cuff of cardigans and jumpers (such as the subtle navy cuff stripe on the Sunset Pink Andean knit) and along the hem edge of hats and scarves.
Orla Daly, CAYO founder, says: “Expanding into the UK market through a premier retailer like Square Bath is such an exciting milestone for CAYO. We set out to create pieces that feel incredible to wear while honouring our commitment to ethical production. By using our custom-spun alpaca yarn, we can offer customers a luxury garment that delivers all the softness of cashmere or mohair, but with far greater durability and easier care. It really is an investment piece designed to be worn and loved season after season.”
The collection is available in-store at Square Bath and online at www.cayo-brand.com / @cayo_the_brand
Pricing ranges from £70-£400.
Square Bath is open Monday-Saturday 10am-6pm and Sunday 10am-5pm. Square Bath: 12 New Bond St, Bath BA1 1BE

items.title: Wickes posts bumper sales but customers put kitchen upgrades on pause as prices rise
items.summary: The DIY retailer said it had seen 'good momentum' in recent months as sales volumes grew as timber, roofing and garden products have boomed.
items.body:
Wickes posts bumper sales but customers put kitchen upgrades on pause as prices rise
Wickes has been boosted by bumper sales even as it warned some customers are pressing pause on bespoke kitchen upgrades as prices start to rise.
The DIY retailer said it had seen ‘good momentum’ in recent months as sales volumes grew as timber, roofing and garden products boomed.
But it said that sales were flat in its design and installation arm as consumer caution hits its bespoke kitchen ranges - which start at around £4,000.
Although there is ‘healthy revenue and volume growth’ in its cheaper ‘lifestyle kitchen’ range of flat-pack ready-to-fit kitchens and bespoke bathrooms, customers are ‘being more considered for larger purchases,’ such as bespoke kitchens.
The London-listed giant also said that ‘mild price inflation’ was starting to filter through ‘after a sustained period of deflation.'
Shares rose 4pc on Tuesday morning after it said total group sales grew 4.5 per cent to £439 million for the three months to 26 September, compared to the same quarter last year.
Kitchen upgrades: Wickes has said customers are pulling pack on pricier home renos
Wickes chief executive David Wood said more customers were choosing the retailer for their home improvement projects. ‘Our continued market share gains demonstrate the strength of our value-led proposition and our ability to outperform in a competitive market,’ he said.
Wickes’ customer reticence over splashing out on pricier kitchens comes after Kingfisher - which owns B&Q and Screwfix - last month said kitchens were doing better than bathrooms.
The retailer said that its summer sales had been hit by a weak demand for its bathroom ranges, while customers forked out on kitchens.
Kingfisher chief executive Thierry Garnier said: ‘People are spending more money on their kitchen today than on their bathroom… a more important part of our lives, it’s becoming a more important room in the house, and we see that across Europe – a more positive trend on kitchen than bathroom.’
AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould said: ‘Where Wickes is faring less well is on the design and installation side where like-for-like revenue was in reverse. This was down to customers being more reluctant to splash out on bespoke kitchens.
‘This is no great shock given the pressure on household finances and Wickes will hope this is spending which might return if or when the backdrop improves.’

Available exclusively at Asda until the end of October, Florette is the […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
UK’s leading fresh salad brand, Florette, is proud to support Breast Cancer Now and CoppaFeel! for the second year running through its limited-edition Tickled Pink Crispy Salad Bag, using its best-selling product to raise awareness and encourage shoppers to support two important causes.
Available exclusively at Asda until the end of October, Florette is the first produce SKU to launch as part of Asda’s 2026 Tickled Pink campaign, alongside 220 other household favourites. The limited-edition pink pack makeover brings instant colour and standout to the ‘sea of green’ in the salad aisle, giving a fresh look to a much-loved product that helped pioneer the prepared salads category in the 1990s.
Following its first year supporting the initiative in 2025, which raised £8,000 for charity, Florette has built on learnings from the campaign by giving its best-known Crispy salad a pink makeover rather than creating a standalone product. This approach aims to reach more shoppers and maximise awareness, while offering fresh, crunchy leaves that are washed and ready to eat for convenient, nutritious everyday lunches.
For every pack sold, 10% of the sale price will be donated directly to Breast Cancer Now and CoppaFeel!, shining a light on breast cancer awareness and helping support their important work. Florette’s influencer campaign has further supported the initiative, encouraging shoppers to get involved, pick up a pack and help spread the word.
Polly Davies, head of category & marketing at Florette, said: “We’re ‘tickled pink’ to be supporting such an important cause for the second year running! Our Crispy salad has been a Florette favourite for decades, so giving our pack an iconic pink makeover felt like the perfect way to add colour to the salad aisle while raising awareness of Breast Cancer Now and CoppaFeel!.
“We’re proud to use a product that helps people make fresh, healthy choices every day to support a cause that matters so much. We’re two weeks into the launch and confident we’ll hit out fundraising target for this year. We hope shoppers will join us in getting behind Tickled Pink, and we’d love to see more brands do the same. By working together and finding creative ways to support important causes, we can spread the word and make a real difference.”
